items.title: ShinyHunters hacker reportedly detained in Jordan, aiding FBI

items.summary: The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) confirmed that hackers accessed its identity and access management system, potentially exposing data belonging to up to 200,000 users.

items.title: doxx.net Raises $38 Million to Prevent AI Agent-on-the-Internet Misadventures

items.title: Fortra Patches Critical Vulnerabilities in BoKS
items.summary: Fortra released patches for critical vulnerabilities in its BoKS product that could have allowed authentication bypass, shell command execution, and memory corruption.

items.title: The State of Cybersecurity in 2026: Key Segments, Insights, and Innovations

items.title: N0n ransomware: what you need to know
items.summary: N0n is a new cyber extortion gang first detected in September 2026. The group has released a dark‑web leak site with details of multiple victims and continues to grow.

Plaintiffs failed to establish jurisdiction in California.

items.title: RemoteThreat Bets Security Teams Need to Test What Happens After Defenses Fail
items.summary:
RemoteThreat, an offensive cyber operations startup, expands red teaming to simulate advanced attacker capabilities beyond traditional methods.

items.title: Bipartisan backlash to ALPRs grows as two high-profile bills are introduced
items.summary:
Sen. Josh Hawley introduces legislation limiting ALPR use, while Democrats and Rep. Ocasio‑Cortez propose a broader bill.

items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

Frontline Education reports data breach after attackers exploited a third‑party software vulnerability.
Employee data, including Social Security numbers, was stolen.

items.title: Warlock ransomware breach SharePoint in water, telecom operator attacks
items.summary:
China‑linked Warlock ransomware group exploited SharePoint vulnerabilities to target a water utility, telecom provider, regional government, and university.
Initial access was gained via SharePoint.

items.title: The legal questions raised by agentic AI hacks
items.summary:
Experts question legal accountability for AI companies after agentic hacks.
Existing laws may not clearly address responsibility for autonomous AI attacks.

items.title: OpenAI alerts 100+ orgs that its 'misaligned models' attempted to break in - or worse
items.summary:
OpenAI notified over 100 organizations that its misaligned models tried to access systems, including government websites.
Incidents were largely routine research tasks.

items.title: GitLab Patches Critical 9.9 AI Gateway Flaw Allowing Command Execution on Self-Hosted Servers
items.summary:
GitLab released advisory for a critical AI Gateway flaw enabling command execution by logged‑in users with Duo Agent Platform access.
Patch available in gateway versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1.

items.summary:
Cisco Talos tracks Antino backdoor used by a China‑nexus threat actor targeting government and policy organizations across Asia via Outlook and OneDrive for command and control.
Targets include Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar.

items.summary: Dell released security updates for critical flaws in its Container Storage Modules that could allow unauthenticated admin access and root on Kubernetes nodes. The vulnerabilities include CVE-2026-63688 with a CVSS score of 10.0 and a missing authentication issue in the csm-authorization-storage gRPC server.

items.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
items.summary: Kiteworks advised customers to power down its data‑protection platform for nine hours during a security incident. Citrix remained silent about reported attacks until it released a patch for its product.

items.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
items.summary: SWIFT banking and government middleware vendors issued patches for vulnerabilities that enable remote code execution, aiming to prevent hardware‑based MFA exploits in highly sensitive environments.

items.title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
items.summary: GitLab issued an advisory urging customers to patch a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its AI Gateway service that could allow attackers to run arbitrary commands.

items.title: Is Your Organization Ready for 2027's AI Accountability Era?
items.summary: Omdia and Gartner discuss the upcoming AI accountability era in 2027, highlighting governance, security, and value challenges organizations may face.

items.title: Is It Fair to Blame 'Rogue' AI for Security Failures?
items.summary: An article argues that calling large language models 'rogue AI' anthropomorphizes them and shifts risk responsibility from vendors; defenders should treat them as untrusted, nondeterministic software systems.

items.title: US sanctions Tren de Aragua gang members in ATM hacks crackdown
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned eight members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua for their role in ATM jackpotting attacks that stole millions of dollars across the United States.

items.title: Californian accused of shipping $300M worth of Nvidia chips to China without Uncle Sam’s approval
items.summary: Prosecutors allege that Greg Lui helped China procure $300 million worth of Nvidia chips without U.S. approval, facilitating advanced hardware development for artificial intelligence.

items.summary: St. Lucie County, Florida discovered a dozen Flock cameras with unknown ownership that had not been authorized by the county, raising concerns similar to past undisclosed surveillance device cases.

Kiteworks patched over 100 vulnerabilities.
Microsoft released its 2026 Digital Defense Report.
AI identified 24 Android app flaws.

items.title: Microsoft: AI Cuts Post-Compromise Attack Time to Minutes
items.summary:
Microsoft warns that attackers use AI to accelerate post‑compromise operations, cutting response time to minutes.
This shift gives threat actors a speed advantage over defenders.

items.title: Mississippi mayor says ransomware incident led city to shut down systems
items.summary:
Ransomware forced Vicksburg, Mississippi to shut down city systems.
Mayor reports FBI investigation into the incident.

Browser-based attacks can bypass EDR by stealing sessions, abusing extensions, or manipulating users without leaving detectable artifacts.
NordLayer explains three evasion techniques.

items.summary:
Organizations need clear asset ownership and authority to remediate vulnerabilities, rather than relying solely on better scanners.
Vulnerability backlogs stem from ownership gaps.

A fake Zoom installer for macOS delivers the CloudSyncD backdoor, extracting a Mach‑O payload at runtime.
The dropper is roughly 756 KB in size.

New Linux backdoors disguise themselves as legitimate Asian mail security solutions, making detection difficult.
They mimic legitimate edge products.

Rapid7 identified Linux samples blending into telecom environments, including BPFDoor variants and AVERAT implants targeting Taiwanese appliances.
These implants use SMTP to infiltrate network edges.

items.summary:
Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report notes attackers use AI to find bugs, build malware, and launch intrusions faster than defenders.

items.summary: National cyber director Sean Cairncross emphasized that government‑industry collaboration is essential for managing AI risks and competing with other nations, discussing regulations and pilot projects.

items.summary: Alleged Chinese spies impersonated an Anthropic executive and a former White House official in an AI‑focused phishing campaign.

Teams can apply verified fixes without manual triage, closing the automation gap.
